# Job Chapter 21 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 423v–424r

---

**21:1** And-answered Iyyov [Job] and-said:

**21:2** "Hear [shim'u], hear [shamo'a] my-word [millati], and-let-this-be [utehi zot] your-consolations [tanchumotekhem]. **21:3** Bear-with-me [sa'uni] and-I will-speak [va'adabber], and-after my-speaking [daberi] you-may-mock [talig].

**21:4** As-for-me [ha-anokhi], to-man [le-adam] [is] my-complaint [sichi]? And-if-so [ve-im maddu'a], why should-my-spirit [ruchi] not-be-short [lo tiqtsar]?

**21:5** Turn [penu] to-me and-be-appalled [vehashimmu], and-lay [vesimu] [your] hand [yad] upon [your] mouth [al peh].

**21:6** And-when I-remember [zacharti] I-am-terrified [venivhalti], and-my-flesh [besari] seizes [achaz] shuddering [pallatsuth].

**21:7** Why [maddua'] do-the-wicked [reshaim] live [yichyu], grow-old [atequ], also [gam] are-mighty [gavru] in-power [chayil]?

**21:8** Their-seed [zar'am] is-established [nakhon] before-them [lifneihem] with-them [immahem], and-their-offspring [ve-etsa'etseihem] before-their-eyes [le-eneihem]. **21:9** Their-houses [batteihem] [are] peace [shalom] without-fear [mippachad], and-the-rod [shevet] of-God [eloah] [is] not upon-them.

**21:10** His-bull [shoro] breeds [ya'abber] and-does-not fail [velo yag'il]; his-cow [parato] calves [tefallete] and-does-not miscarry [velo teshakkel].

**21:11** They-send-out [yeshalechu] like-the-flock [katson] their-little-ones [avileihem], and-their-children [yaldeihem] dance [yeraqqedun]. **21:12** They-lift-up [yis'u] [the] tambourine [ketof] and-harp [khinnor], and-they-rejoice [veyismechu] at-the-sound of-the-pipe [ugav].

**21:13** They-spend [yekhalu] in-prosperity [batov] their-days [yemeihem], and-in-a-moment [uverega'] to-Sheol [she'ol] they-go-down [yechatu].

**21:14** And-they-say [vayyomeru] to-God [la-el], 'Depart [sur] from-us; and-knowledge [da'at] of-your-ways [derakhekha] we-do-not desire [lo chafatsnu].' **21:15** What [mah] [is] Shaddai that-we-should-serve-him [ki na'avdennu]? And-what profit [mah nissa] if-we-pray-to-him [ki nifga' bo]?'

**21:16** Behold, not in-their-hand [beyadam] [is] their-prosperity [tuvam] — the-counsel [atsat] of-the-wicked [reshaim] is-far [rachaqah] from-me.

**21:17** How-often [kammah] [is] the-lamp [ner] of-the-wicked [reshaim] extinguished [yid'akh]? And-comes [yavo] upon-them their-destruction [eidam]? Pains [chavalim] he-distributes [yechalleq] in-his-anger [be-appo]?

**21:18** They-are [yihyu] like-straw [keteven] before [lifnei] the-wind [ruach], and-like-chaff [khamots] that-the-storm [se'arah] steals-away [genavato]?

**21:19** God [eloah] stores-up [yitspon] for-his-sons [levanav] his-trouble [ono]; let-him-repay [yeshallem] him [eilav] and-he-will-know [veyeda].

**21:20** Let-his-own-eyes [einav] see [yir'u] his-downfall [kido], and-from-the-wrath [umichemat] of-Shaddai let-him-drink [yishhteh].

**21:21** For what [ki mah] [is] his-pleasure [cheftso] in-his-house [beveito] after-him [acharav], when-the-number [umispar] of-his-months [chodashav] is-cut-off [chutsetsu]?

**21:22** To-God [la-el] will-one-teach [yelamded] knowledge [da'at], and-he [who] judges [yishpot] the-exalted-ones [ramim]?

**21:23** This-one [zeh] dies in-the-fullness [be-etsem] of-his-perfection [tummo], wholly at-ease [shalanan] and-secure [shalev]. **21:24** His-pails [atinaiv] are-full [male'u] of-milk [chalav], and-the-marrow [umoach] of-his-bones [atsmotav] is-moist [yeshaqeh].

**21:25** And-this-one [ve-zeh] dies in-bitterness of-soul [bemarath nefesh], and-has-not tasted [velo akhal] good [batovah].

**21:26** Together [yachad] upon the-dust [al afar] they-lie-down [yishkabu], and-worms [rimmah] cover-them [tekasseh aleihem].

**21:27** Behold, I-know [yadati] your-thoughts [machshevotekhem], and-the-devices [umezimmot] [with which] you-do-violence [tachmesu] against-me.

**21:28** For you-say [tomeru], 'Where [ayyeh] [is] the-house [beit] of-the-noble [nadiv]? And-where [ve-ayyeh] [is] the-tent [ohel], the-dwelling [mishkenot] of-the-wicked [reshaim]?'

**21:29** Have-you-not asked [ha-lo she'altem] the-travelers [overei derekh], and-their-signs [ve-ototam] you-will-not recognize [tekkeru]?

**21:30** That the-evil [ra'] man is-spared [yechasekh] for-the-day of-destruction [le-yom eid]? For-the-day of-wrath [le-yom averot] they-are-led-away [yuvallu]?

**21:31** Who declares [yaggid] to-his-face [al panav] his-way [darkho]? And-what he-has-done [hu asah], who repays [yeshallem] to-him?

**21:32** And-he is-carried [yuval] to-the-graves [liqvarot], and-over the-tomb [gadish] he-keeps-watch [yishqod].

**21:33** Sweet [matqu] to-him [are] the-clods [rigvei] of-the-valley [nachal]; and-after-him [ve-acharav] every man [kol adam] draws [yimshokh], and-before-him [velefanav] [are] without number [ein mispar].

**21:34** And-how [ve-eikh] will-you-comfort-me [tenachamuni] [with] emptiness [hevel]? And-your-answers [uteshuvotekhem] — there-remains [nish'ar] unfaithfulness [ma'al]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.7 — "Why do the wicked live?":** The most direct challenge to retribution theology in the entire book. Job does not merely say the wicked sometimes prosper — he describes them thriving in every dimension: long life, wealth, healthy livestock, happy children, music, peaceful death.

**v.13 — "in a moment to Sheol they go down":** The wicked die quickly and painlessly — the opposite of what the friends claim. This is not judgment; it is mercy. Job is pointing out the scandal: the wicked get an easy death.

**v.17 — "How often?":** Job uses the rhetorical question to challenge Bildad's claim (18:5) that the lamp of the wicked is extinguished. His implied answer: rarely.

**v.22 — "Will one teach God knowledge?":** Job silences the friends' pretension — who are they to explain God's ways? The same God who judges the exalted ones (*ramim*, possibly celestial beings) cannot be schooled by human theologians.

**v.30 — Interpretive crux:** This verse can be read two ways: (a) the wicked are spared/reserved for the day of destruction, or (b) the wicked are spared on the day of destruction. The ambiguity is crucial — Job may be saying the wicked are kept safe even when calamity strikes.

*— EMET*
